prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP Manifesto 2017 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core message: Deliver a “real Brexit,” restore sovereignty, cut immigration, rebalance the economy toward British workers and communities, invest in public services without raising taxes, and restructure UK democracy.

Brexit and sovereignty
- Leave the EU as fast as possible; prefer repeal of the 1972 European Communities Act over Article 50 bargaining.
- Six Brexit tests: legal sovereignty (no ECJ/ECHR jurisdiction), full border/migration control, restore 200‑mile EEZ and fisheries, independent trade policy (leave single market/customs union; WTO-ready), no divorce bill and recover UK assets, complete exit by end-2019.
- Fisheries: withdraw from CFP and the 1964 London Convention; rebuild fleet; end discards; require UK landing; license limited foreign access during transition.

Economy, tax, and funding
- Finance priorities from £35bn savings: cut foreign aid to 0.2% GNI and close DFID; scrap HS2; replace Barnett Formula with needs-based system; end EU budget payments; other efficiencies.
- No tax rises; raise personal allowance to £13,500 and 40% threshold to £55,000; raise inheritance tax threshold to £500,000 each (goal: abolish); remove VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaway food; abolish TV licence over 3 years; crack down on multinational tax avoidance.
- Cut business rates 20% for premises <£50k RV; protect self-employed from NI hikes/quarterly returns; open procurement to SMEs; late payment fines.

Communities, housing and transport
- Coastal Enterprise Zones with halved business rates; targeted regeneration and housing standards enforcement.
- Housing: create a Housing Development Corporation to build up to 100,000 high‑quality factory‑built modular homes/year on brownfield; sold freehold to under‑40 first‑time buyers with resale to HDC.
- Scrap HS2; oppose Heathrow third runway; remove road tolls; protect diesel owners from new penalties; expand EV rapid charging; support regional airports; freeze/aim to scrap APD.

NHS and social care
- Extra £9bn/yr for NHS and £2bn/yr for social care by 2021/22; integrate health and care in a new department.
- Lift cap on medical school places; pay tuition for doctors (NHS service commitment) and abolish tuition fees for STEM (work-in-UK commitment); restore nurse bursaries; more GPs/nurses; cut red tape.
- Tougher action on ineligible overseas use; manager licensing; end PFI; guarantee rights of EU health/care workers.

Mental health, education, families
- +£500m/yr for mental health; 28‑day maximum wait; school-based counselling; stronger perinatal access.
- Education: a grammar or technical school in every town; stronger vocational/dual training; restore maintenance grants; abolish tuition fees for STEM; end primary sex ed; improve careers/employability.
- Childcare: extend school day (8–6 wraparound); deregulate access to providers; £80m fund to include children with special needs.
- Family courts: transparency; presumptive shared parenting; grandparents’ contact rights.

Elderly, disability and carers
- Keep pensioner benefits and triple lock; invest up to £2bn/yr in social care; ban zero-hours for home care; £400m/yr dementia research; reform PIP/WCA; raise Carer’s Allowance; scrap bedroom tax.

Immigration and integration
- Target net migration to zero over five years; Australian-style points plus work permits; five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration; seasonal visas; 4,000 extra Border Force staff; no amnesty; five-year qualification for welfare/NHS (non-urgent).
- Integration: “one law for all”; plan to disband sharia councils; ban face coverings in public; zero tolerance of FGM, forced marriage, “honour” crimes; tough Ofsted action against Islamist influence.

Law and order
- 20,000 more police; restore stop-and-search; 7,000 more prison officers; tougher prisons, anti-radicalisation, foreign prisoners repatriation; opt out of the European Arrest Warrant; repeal Labour-era human rights law and enact a UK Bill of Rights.

Defence and foreign policy
- Genuine 2% of GDP on defence plus £1bn/yr by 2021/22; rebuild forces (+20,000), fix procurement; veterans’ administration, housing, jobs, legal protections; retain nuclear deterrent; cautious on interventions; pro‑NATO/Five Eyes; conditional engagement with Russia; pro‑US/UK trade deal.
- Foreign aid cut to 0.2% GNI; “trade not aid”; commission a 500‑bed hospital ship for humanitarian/defence support.

Environment, farming and energy
- New UK Environmental Protection Act; protect ancient woodlands; focus on brownfield; tackle plastic bottle waste; enable dredging to prevent floods.
- Agriculture: UK Single Farm Payment with £120k cap; support small/hill/organic farms; stricter animal welfare (CCTV in abattoirs, live export ban for slaughter, method-of-slaughter labelling).
- Energy: repeal Climate Change Act; leave Paris/EU ETS; diversify supply incl. shale (not in national parks); cut green levies/VAT on fuel; review utilities’ profits.

Constitution and localism
- Abolish House of Lords; create English Parliament (proportional system); halve Commons to 325 (PR); citizens’ initiative with binding referenda; restrict postal voting to need; local binding referenda; keep council tax low.
